justification: Explicitly a review demonstrating mostly animal-model findings (catalepsy, spatial memory in mice), not a primary human study.
Observational study of marijuana use and verbal learning/delayed recall in young adults using validated CogState list-learning test.
Systematic review and meta-analysis of CB1 receptor compounds across species, not a primary empirical study.
Meta-analysis pooling neurocognition studies of cannabis-using psychosis patients, not primary research.
Experimental fMRI crossover with acute THC and a verbal learning task measuring hippocampal encoding in healthy males.
Longitudinal study linking adolescent cannabis use to change in working memory and neurocognitive function.
Study examines binge drinking and episodic memory; cannabis only a controlled confounder, not the characterized exposure.
Compares synthetic cannabinoid and cannabis users on n-back working memory and free-recall memory tasks.
Cross-sectional study of heavy cannabis use before psychosis with neurocognitive testing including episodic memory.
Proposes a novel research agenda/treatment strategy for marijuana addiction; a review/commentary, not primary research.
